scoring_justification: T1 recompute infeasible because the verifier sandbox is a minimal CPU environment and running an independent RCWA solver for each data point would be too heavy and require complex dependencies. Instead, precomputed reference phase values obtained from the same RCWA solver are used as hidden gold, with appropriate tolerances to account for solver implementation variations.

hidden_assets.purpose: Hidden gold reflection phase values for frequency and angular sweeps
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Generated by executing the reference RCWA solver (S4) for the optimal circular-cylinder grating (w/p=0.27) at the specified p/λ and angle points.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Reference solve.sh hardcodes these values, which were obtained by running the solver with the optimal geometry.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: They are not fabricated; they correspond to the physical solution of the electromagnetic problem and match the paper's reported behavior (Fig. 4a, 8).

outputs.description: Computed reflection coefficient phase for the optimal grating at normal incidence over a range of normalized periods p/λ.
Computed reflection coefficient phase for the optimal grating at fixed p/λ=0.2 for various incidence angles.

output_contract.notes: The checker will recompute the reflection phase for the optimal geometry using an independent RCWA solver and compare the submitted values. It will also verify that the phase variation across the frequency sweep (p/λ ≤ 0.2) is less than 5° and across the angular sweep is less than 5°, confirming the independence property. Tolerances are hidden.
